conflicts.description: The skybridge lattice can only be renewed if rites are performed at anchors on every isle, but anchor sovereignty forbids outsiders from acting. The Stormwardens demand recognition of their supremacy, the Chartwrights demand free access, and neither will yield while the spans burn away strand by strand.
conflicts.name: The Deadlock of Anchors

conflicts.description: The Silkwind Compact has learned that certain skybridge failures were induced — and rather than expose the saboteur, it sells safe-passage tokens around the failing spans. Reunification would end both the sabotage and the Compact's fortune, so Vessala quietly works to keep the enclaves divided.
conflicts.name: The Quiet Profiteering

conflicts.description: A true chart of the drift would prove the failures form a deliberate spiral aimed at Calythra's keystone heartstone. The guild elders suppressed the finding once; a young cartographer who redraws it must choose between the oath and the guild, and carry the map to enclaves that will each find reason to call it a forgery.
conflicts.name: The Map No One Wants

description: Long ago the continent of Aeloria shattered and rose into the heavens, becoming an archipelago of floating isles adrift on the wind-currents of the upper air. The isles are held in constellation by the skybridges — living lattices of bound starlight anchored to each island's heartstone, woven in an age when the enclaves still spoke to one another. Now the lattices are fraying. Whole spans dim and unravel strand by strand, and islands at the archipelago's edge have begun to wander toward the Abyssal Maw, the churning storm-gulf below from which nothing returns. The enclaves — proud, suspicious, and long divided by the Concord that once bound them — each blame the others for the decay, and each hoards its fragment of the old knowledge needed for the renewal rites. Into this drifting world steps a young cartographer of Auravale, whose charts reveal a truth no enclave will admit: the drift is accelerating, the pattern of failures is not natural, and unless the rival isles are persuaded to share anchor-rite and heartstone alike, Aeloria will scatter forever into the Maw. It is a world of wonder — cloud-whales gliding beneath translucent spans, wind-sailed skiffs, lantern-lit markets hung from island undersides — and of quiet dread, for every map the guild draws is already wrong by the time the ink dries.

factions.description: Auravale's guild of mapmakers, oathbound to chart the truth of the drifting isles. In practice the guild hoards its maps as political leverage, and its elders suppress evidence that the skybridge failures follow a deliberate pattern.
factions.name: The Chartwright Guild

factions.description: Ondrel's hereditary order of weather-singers who maintain the wards against the Abyssal Maw. They claim storm-song can mend a fraying skybridge, but refuse to share the rite unless the other enclaves acknowledge their sovereignty over all anchors.
factions.name: The Stormwardens

factions.description: Vessala's consortium of traders and toll-keepers. The Compact profits handsomely from enclave isolation and quietly discourages any reunification that would make its toll-tokens worthless — even as the crossings it taxes grow perilous.
factions.name: The Silkwind Compact

factions.description: A dwindling monastic order on Calythra that once performed the renewal rites on every skybridge in the archipelago. Now reduced to a handful of aging keepers, they alone know that the lattice's unraveling began the day the Concord of Anchors broke.
factions.name: The Spanwardens

history.description: The heartstone beneath old Aeloria cracked in a cataclysm no chronicle fully explains, and the continent tore itself into hundreds of isles that rose into the sky. Countless souls were lost to the Maw before the survivors learned to live aloft.
history.name: The Sundering

history.description: On Calythra, the first Spanwardens bound starlight into a living span and anchored it to a neighboring isle, proving the archipelago could be held together. Enclave by enclave, the lattice grew over the following generations.
history.name: The Weaving of the First Skybridge

history.description: Fearing conquest by bridge, the enclaves signed the Concord granting each sole authority over its own anchors, with the Spanwardens chartered as neutral keepers of the renewal rites. It bought two centuries of peace — and planted the seed of the present crisis.
history.name: The Concord of Anchors

history.description: When the isle of Pelagios refused renewal rites over a toll dispute, its last skybridge parted in a storm and the whole isle drifted into the Abyssal Maw. The enclaves mourned, blamed one another, and changed nothing.
history.name: The Loss of Far Pelagios

history.description: Invited onto fewer and fewer isles, the Spanwardens withdrew to Calythra and fell silent. The renewal rites went unperformed across the lattice, and the first dimming of the skybridges began — slow enough that each enclave could pretend not to see it.
history.name: The Hush of the Wardens

locations.description: The largest of the drifting isles and seat of the Chartwright Guild, Auravale is a terraced plateau of windmill orchards and observatory spires. Its underdocks hum with skiff traffic, and its great Mapparium holds the only near-complete chart of the skybridge lattice — a chart that grows less true with each passing season.
locations.name: Auravale

locations.description: A merchant isle hung with lantern-lit bazaars on both its crown and its underside, Vessala controls the toll-tokens that grant passage across the busiest skybridge crossings. Its Silkwind traders grow rich ferrying goods between enclaves that refuse to deal with one another directly.
locations.name: Vessala

locations.description: A craggy storm-wracked isle on the archipelago's windward edge, Ondrel is home to the Stormwardens, whose weather-wards shield the inner isles from the Maw's lightning. Their ancestors claimed the skybridges answered to storm-song, a secret they guard jealously.
locations.name: Ondrel

locations.description: The oldest isle, where the first skybridge was anchored and where the Spanwardens keep their silent vigil. Calythra's heartstone is the keystone of the entire lattice; its shrine-towers are carved with the renewal rites, worn smooth by centuries of neglect.
locations.name: Calythra

name: Aeloria, the Fractured Sky

rules.name: The Living Lattice
rules.statement: Each skybridge is a living lattice of bound starlight, not a structure of stone or steel. It frays when its anchor-rites go unperformed and cannot be repaired by craft alone — only by the renewal rites that no single enclave still fully remembers.

rules.name: The Law of Drift
rules.statement: Every island drifts on the wind-currents. A skybridge anchored to an island's heartstone holds it in constellation with its neighbors; an island that loses all its bridges wanders steadily toward the Abyssal Maw and is lost.

rules.name: Wind, Sinew, and Crystal
rules.statement: All craft in Aeloria runs on wind-sails, heartstone resonance, and grown crystal mechanisms. No combustion engines or explosive arts exist; the air itself is too rich in starlight static for open flame beyond the hearth.

rules.name: Anchor Sovereignty
rules.statement: Under the Concord of Anchors, each enclave holds sole authority over the skybridge anchors on its soil. No outsider may perform rites at another enclave's anchor without invitation — a law now strangling the renewal the lattice needs.

rules.name: The Cartographer's Oath
rules.statement: Every Chartwright swears to map what is true, not what is convenient. To falsify a chart or hide a drift-reading is oathbreak — yet the guild's elders weigh the oath against the panic a true map would unleash.
